items.english: In return, she left no itch unscratched and showed him every indulgence.
"The Living-Rope house's guard, Isogai Sensei, is a greater man than Hirate Miki at Sasagawa Shigezo's, whose name lives on in stories to this day."
notes: Speaker not named in the text; taken as O-Tetsu's boast to others, lifting Ryujiro as her house swordsman. Sensei kept for the irony.

items.english: Lift him as high as they would, in truth it was no different from being locked in gaol.
"If I go on like this, I can never face Akioka Sensei."

His soul had not rotted through entirely. Unable to bear the pricks of conscience, he seized the opening he had at last found and, from the back garden of O-Tetsu's house, clinging to the wild grass, climbed down the cliff to the path between the rice fields in the valley.

Before he had time to think how glad he was, a snare fell from above with a snap. It caught him from under his left arm to over his right shoulder and, with a sharp tightening, he was fished straight up. His body hung in midair.
"Sensei, why do such a thing? Whatever happens, I shall never let you escape."
Above him O-Tetsu's voice, pitched high with rage, rang and rang.

O-Tetsu, returned by the narrowest chance, had stopped Ryujiro's flight with a ready thrown rope. She bound him up in a high-hands, small-hands tie and left him tumbled in the back loft, and beside him, gulping teacup sake in spite, she opened her mouth as if full of regret.
notes: Takade-kote rendered literally to keep the binding vocabulary; first-use gloss left to the catalogue passage.

items.english: "Why, Sensei, did you try to run? In the little while I let my watch slip... And I had not gone out on other business either. From the pool at Sugatsu I went to fetch sesame eels to give you whole-boiled and put a little strength into you, and that from my own single heart, without leaving it to other hands. And to think of this."
